magellan_marauder_1.job_description:
The bounty link directs you to a Magellan officer. "Thought I'd find you here," he says, "I'm ==Morik Kiderra==, Blackcollar Regiment. Your reputation precedes you. Much as I hate to admit it, I'm in a bit of a... political bind," he says with a grimace. "Not too long ago, the merchant guilds, Tichel especially, kicked up a fuss about losing shipping to piracy. Fleet was strongarmed into taking action and I was assigned a mission to neutralize the target: a former Blackcollar engineer by name of ==Tai Cor-Lan== leading a group called the ==Marauders==," he says with a disdain, "We cornered and destroyed much of their fleet, though their leaders escaped and went to ground - and anyone with half a brain knows they'll be back soon enough."
"But for some damn reason, Fleet considers the matter closed and redeployed my forces despite vocal complaints from both myself and the merchant guilds, probably because it was politically motivated to begin with." he says, throwing up his hands helplessly. "Yes, good soldiers follow orders, but as a good soldier I can't let this go unresolved, especially with a deserter on the loose. Unfortunately, I'm on the side of Tichel," he says with a grin, all too aware of the irony, "and they've agreed to have it handled unofficially."
"So, here I am, the apolitical soldier with a political agenda. I provide intelligence and information while Tichel backs it up with credits." He flips a PDA your way, "I've tracked down and located part of scattered remnants, a group of stragglers lead by ==$name==, who's known to pilot a ==heavily-modified Bastardsword-class Corvette==. You won't get much in the way of official recognition for this, but the information is accurate and the reward is good. What do you say?"
magellan_marauder_1.job_comm_reply: The image comes in, lightly speckled by radiation. The pirate barely takes one look at you before storming off-screen, shouting obscenities. As their chair spins idly in feed, you hear $himHerThem raging in the background about getting shafted by the Herdmaster if $heSheThey loses his favorite corvette.
magellan_marauder_1.job_intel_success:
On sending proof of the death of the target, you promptly receive a wire for the agreed upon amount, along with a comms request from ==Morik Kiderra==.
"I'm still reviewing the footage, but it looks good. I've confirmed it with Tichel, and they've agreed to release your reward." He looks down and scrolls through a few pages on his PDA, "I've got another lead when you have the chance. It appears the next target has fled much further than this one, either to put distance between themselves and Khamn, or for some other unknown reason. It'd be good to get this done and dusted sooner rather than later." He gives you a nod, and signs off.

magellan_marauder_2.job_description:
The bounty link directs you to the same Blackcollar officer as before. "Excellent job on that last mission," Kiderra says with a nod, "their lieutenant is dead and the rest destroyed or scattered. In other news, Fleet is still being obstinate and refuses to recognize the problem," he says with a sigh, "So the plan continues. This next set of stragglers took a bit of finding, but their poor comsec gave them away."
He flips a PDA your way. "This fragment is lead by ==$name==, who's known to pilot a ==heavily-modified Jitte-class Fighter==. Interestingly, they've moved into the Core - I can only imagine they tried to get away from our prying eyes to pick up reinforcements. While they haven't managed the former, they seem to have gotten involved with the local warlords, worryingly enough." His eyes tighten, "Nothing good can come of Kanta's involvement in Magellan affairs, so deal with this quickly. Tichel understand the concerning nature of this develpoment, and have increased their reward accordingly. What do you say?"
magellan_marauder_2.job_comm_reply: $name looks at you, and a grin splits $hisHerTheir greasy face, "Ah, ye must be Kiderra's dog what took down our best corvette pilot. But do what ye will, we've already won - Kanta's got her pound of flesh." The link cuts off with a snap.
magellan_marauder_2.job_intel_success:
On sending proof of the death of the target, you promptly receive a wire for the agreed upon amount, along with a comms request from ==Morik Kiderra==.
He appears worried as the link opens, "The pirate captain's statements are... concerning, to say the least. I can't verify them at the moment, but fleeing to the Core to set up some sort of rendezvous between Kanta's ilk and the Herdmaster is too troubling not to follow up on. In the mean time, Tichel have released your reward. Find me again later, in the usual spot." Kiderra looks pensive as the connection cuts.

magellan_marauder_3.job_description:
The bounty link directs you to the same Blackcollar officer as before. Despite your success, he seems worried. "Another one dead and gone, but things are developing quickly. $name has resurfaced, but more than that, a worrying collaboration appears to have formed. Comms intercepts indicate that $name has brought $hisHerTheir boss, ==Herdmaster Rico 'Brisket' Warrik==, to meet with one of Kanta's brood, ==Warlord Petros Nye==." Kiderra drums his fingers, "With the supply situation as it is, the last thing the Protectorate needs is more pirates plying the trade routes, especially one of Kanta's caliber."
"Fleet have finally got their own head out of their arse and realized the severity of the situation, but by time they get a strike force together, it'll be too late. Tichel Mercantile Concern are still pushing on their end, though," he adds, with a roll of his eyes, "probably because it affects their bottom line, and not the billions of citizens on Khamn."
He flips a PDA your way. "There's a lot of concentrated firepower in this fleet. Not only are the Marauders present, so is the Kantan Warboss's honor guard as well as the Herdmaster's own bodyguard. Leading it all is ==$name== at the helm of the ==$shipName==, a ==heavily-modified Edger-class carrier==. For what it's worth though, you're likely to earn the approval of Fleet for taking down such a high-profile threat. What do you say?
magellan_marauder_3.job_comm_reply: The comms feed flickers as $name appears on screen. "You know, I left the Fleet to avoid this sort of intrigue. You're as much as tool as Kiderra is, getting worked over by the political machine for the benefit of the merchant guilds," he says with a chuckle, but his face hardens. "Normally I'd share some sympathy for you, but you've gone and killed two of my best officers, and interrupted what was a fine meeting. I won't let you off easily."
magellan_marauder_3.job_intel_success:
Not long after the conclusion of the battle, you promptly receive a wire for the agreed upon amount, along with a comms request from ==Morik Kiderra==.
"You've done a fine job out there. While we don't know exact details," he begins explaining, "it seems the Herdmaster was prepared to exchange some of their unique technology in return for support from Kanta, until you put paid to those plans. And along with the reward from Tichel, you've won the recognition of the Fleet. Should you feel inclined, I've given you my ==contact information== - we can always use help from Starfarers like you," he says with approval.
Kiderra looks off thoughtfully, "I hope Tichel doesn't think I owe them after this," he says with a bemused look, "I can't wash my hands of this mess soon enough."
"Oh, and before you go," he adds, "Fleet has also taken some notes based on the Marauders, and begun some combat trials. You've been formally invited to participate, though they insist you do so at your own expense," he finishes with a wry smile.
==Morik Kiderra== added as a ==Potential Contact==

magellan_theghost.job_description:
The bounty link directs you to a nervous-looking scientist. "Oh! Captain. I'm wondering if you could help me with something... unusual here," he asks, taking out a PDA, "I represent the Magellan research station on Pariya. Last month, a long-range patrol did a routine sensor burst in hyperspace which attracted a ==sensor ghost== - it appeared to observe them for a moment before leaving. The patrol went on to complete its round and reported back without issue. But a Fleet intelligence officer going over post-operational data picked up that the ghost actually exited hyperspace near the ==$system== system. One of our scientists confirmed it."
He looks up with incredulity, "I've never seen anything like this. Naturally, we've been pestering Fleet day and night to have this investigated further, but Fleet are keeping a death grip on their fuel reserves, and another patrol isn't scheduled to go out there for the better part of a cycle." He lowers is voice and says, "The nature of this encounter means Fleet would like to keep it off official, public channels to avoid attracting attention from... a certain research institute." You get the idea that the Protectorate does not appreciate the Galatia Academy meddling in local affairs. The scientists continues, "Would you go out there and investigate it on behalf of the Fleet? Our research division is offering a substantial reward."
magellan_theghost.job_comm_reply:
From a great distance, the sensor ghost resolves itself into a ship, as cold and dead as the grave. While it bears the distinctive silhouette of a Mazian-class Dreadnaught, the tactical computer churns and spits out a designation you've never seen before - Duncan-class Dreadnought. As your fleet moves in for a closer inspection, the dreadnaught's weapons and engines power up, prompting an uncomfortable flutter across the bridge.

You hail the ship, but it's already transmitting over an open frequency. An indecipherable video feed comes through, alongside a hopelessly garbled audio track. As your comms officer futilely attempts to dial it in, you feel you make out a faint melody in the chaos, but it escapes almost as soon as you're conscious of it. Your comms officer cuts the connection with a defeated sigh.
magellan_theghost.job_intel_success:
After the destruction of the vessel, your sensors officer quietly reports that no escape pods were detected leaving the vessel at any point. A volunteer salvor team moves in warily as you watch their progress from the bridge. Within they find all the hallmarks of a once-occupied ship - personal belongings, tableware, misplaced tools, and even a highly-corrupted manifest - but no crew, nor in fact any trace of biological matter. Your chief medical officer makes a quip about the sterilty of the operating theater, but the bridge is in quiet shock otherwise. You order a thorough scan of the vessel, the surrounding space, and any relevant items of interest your sensors officer and chief engineer deem appropriate, then send the data package on its way.
Some time later, you receive a wire to your account for the agreed upon amount, in addition to a comms request from the scientist you met earlier. He appears visibly disturbed, "This is, or was, the FSS Warspite. She suffered a poor hyperspace translation and was presumed lost with all hands... several centuries ago." He forces a weak smile, "The rest of the researchers are excited of course, but I think I'd appreciate it if I didn't have to learn anything else about this than I already do. Not that I could anyway, since Fleet has slapped a security level on this so high that I can't even see the bottom of it." As his hand hovers over the disconnect button, he adds, "Be careful out there."

magellan_waywardscion.job_description:
After wading through the pomp that suffocates this message, you manage to decipher its contents. It appears one of the Voscune family heirs has taken their rebellious streak too far to tolerate any further, and has created no amount of problems for the family's prestige. Charges of conspiracy, arms smuggling, and sedition among others have been levelled upon ==$name==, staining the honor and reputation of House Voscune. He promptly defected to the ==Levellers==, taking with him a group of like-minded radicals. He is also known to have received aid from influential associates within ==Dassault-Mikoyan Engineering==, whose involvement within Protectorate affairs would bring no end of trouble were it to be made public.
Your instructions, presented bluntly, are to eliminate their wayward scion before he can make good his plans, or worse yet, be brought in for trial, which would only prolong and further publicize the Voscune family's perilous position.
magellan_waywardscion.job_intel_success:
As the battle comes to a close, your comms officer intercepts an encrypted outgoing message from one of the hulks littering the field. Before you can act however, your tactical officer reports a power surge and subsequent explosion from the same source. Your ops chief scrambles a shuttle to search the hulk - they find the crew are dead, but within a console spared by the surge is the unencrypted message along with a physical UPC for a ==Bastardsword [LV] Corvette==. No doubt the intended recipients will have gotten a copy of it.
Following a short, though grim, expedition into the remnants of the flagship, the target is found and confirmed dead. On sending evidence to the provided darknet address, you promptly receive a wire for the agreed upon amount. No thank-you or words of appreciation, however - it seems the great Houses of Annore show little gratitude for having their dirty work done by an outsider.
magellan_waywardscion.job_comm_reply: The video feed comes in clear and crisp. "I know who sent you. They really must want me dead, to have an outsider do the job..." he says with a wistful look, "It's almost flattering. But I know where I stand, and I won't feed that machine any longer. I won't let go of my hope to make a better society, and if you agree, you'll make like you never saw us."

magellan_dunerunner.job_description:
The bounty link directs you to a dark corner of the bar, where you find an agent sitting in the gloom with a bottle of something strong close at hand. "Hello Captain. Have a seat. Drink?" You take a seat, but politely decline the drink. "Oh, very well. I'll cut to the chase then," she says as she wakes her PDA and turns on the privacy field."I'm an agent representing the ==Association of Interstellar Mercenaries==, AIM. But I'm not here to sell you a mercenary," she says as she catches you getting up, "I'm here to give you a bounty."
"A client hired out a ==Dunerunner== detail under AIM to accompany him on a tech-mining expedition." The agent continues, "They returned, sans client, a few months later saying he had terminated their contract, complete with verification. However, it later came to light that they had turned on the client for something valuable he had found, stole it, and left him for dead. When AIM was informed of the betrayal, they moved swiftly to terminate their contract with the Dunerunner organization, but their legal department shielded them from punishment, instead throwing this fleet under the bus."
"AIM doesn't like these incidents going public, but what it doesn't like more are contract-breakers." She picks up the bottle and weighs it in her hand, "The client didn't make it, but among his final wishes was the transfer of a sum of credits towards a bounty on the head of his betrayer. AIM has also added to it, totalling ==$reward==. It might not be much, but you can't get their ==mod-ships== anywhere else, and it's likely they're still carrying ==valuable cargo== from that tech-mining run. Sound reasonable?"
magellan_dunerunner.job_comm_reply: "I know what you're here for. You ain't getting that Forge from me!"
magellan_dunerunner.job_intel_success: During the post-battle salvage operation, your crews find a nanoforge - the obvious cause of the betrayal. It must have been a Pristine Nanoforge not long ago, but after poor storage conditions, lack of maintenance, and a close encounter with at least two flux core explosions, it's a miracle the forge is still in servicable condition. Though the prize may have been ruined, your chief engineer assures you it will still function properly when slotted into the correct industry. Other than the forge, your salvage teams also pick out a number of valuable items from that ill-fated tech-mining expedition, in addition to their unique ==mod-ships==.
